svg.title: desktop-cracker
svg.desc: An installed desktop-cracker: the package on disk, the names on the PATH, the two programs of a run and the guest they carry, and the lifecycle of one run from the launcher to the machine ending itself.
svg.text: desktop-cracker
a microVM desktop, installed and running — README.md has the detail
Where it is installed
~/desktop-cracker/
or any folder it was extracted into — it runs from there
bin/
desktop-cracker · desk-disk · firecracker
libraries/
the shared libraries that travel with it
kernel/
kernel · initramfs.gz
images/
rootfs.ext4 — the userland a new disk is made from
disks/
root.raw — the encrypted root disk
config.yml
the settings — the settings window edits this file
icons/ · docs/ · VERSION
install.sh · uninstall.sh · launcher.sh
what is linked into the PATH
desk-run
→ launcher.sh → bin/desktop-cracker
desk-disk
→ the disk tool: make, resize, re-key, inspect
One run's life
the user starts it
desk-run, or the desktop entry
it reads its own folder
config.yml · disks/root.raw · kernel/ · images/
it asks for the passphrase
typed by the user, kept in memory, never written
it opens its own run directory
every channel's socket, before the machine starts
it starts firecracker
a child process it defines the machine to, over its API
the desktop appears
the guest boots; the window shows its screen
it ends, and takes it all with it
the guest reboots; the run directory goes away
What a run is made of
desktop-cracker
one process — the whole host side of a run
the window
the guest's screen, at the guest's resolution or full screen;
the global keys; the settings window and every dialog
one service per guest device
display · audio · shared folders · network
remote X · control · shutdown · readiness
each on a thread of its own, each on its own port
the plugin seam (--plugin-path)
what a test watches: milestones, state, screen, questions
desk-run
the launcher on the PATH: starts the application beside it
desk-disk
a disk job in a microVM of its own: create, rootdisk,
resize, change-pass, info — no root, no loop device
the run's own directory
$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/desktop-cracker/run-<pid>/
api.sock — firecracker's API
v.sock · v.sock_53000 … — one socket per channel
control/ — the run's files for the guest, and the guest's back
private to this user, removed when the run ends
reaches, on this machine
the keyboard and the pointer, while the window is focused
the sound device, while the window is visible and numlock is held
the internet, through this process's own network
the X server, for the guest's applications (remote X)
firecracker
a released binary, a child of the application —
github.com/firecracker-microvm/firecracker
the machine is defined over its API: boot source, drives,
vsock, balloon, InstanceStart — an HTTP call each
tied to its parent: if the application dies it dies with it
(PR_SET_PDEATHSIG) — a machine is never an orphan
it serves the guest's devices over one virtio-vsock
the guest — a microVM with KVM
its own kernel and its own memory, gone with the run
desk-agent
the guest's own half: the screen and its damage logic, the
sound, the shares, the network, the run's files, the way out
the disks
root.raw — a LUKS container, opened inside the guest with the
passphrase the user typed: the host holds no key for it
additional disks as /dev/vdb…, mounted by the guest's user
the guest's desktop
Debian 12: LightDM + Xfce, VLC, Firefox, Python 3.13
the host's folders mounted, its own sshd and its own tun0
it reaches its own session with no password
API
vsock
kernel
how it ends
the window's Close: the guest reboots itself, firecracker exits
the application is killed: the child dies with it
F9 hides the window, and the password brings it back
whichever way it ended: the run's directory is gone, and the guest with it
a process
a channel
encrypted
a disk
this machine
make architecture prints this file's path · make help lists every command
